cases.rendered:
In the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, a small business is a business that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with a total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Under that definition, a business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

In the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, a small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under that definition, a business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Gross turnover means the gross inflow of economic benefits during the period arising in the course of the operating activities of an entity when those inflows result in increases in equity, including sales of goods, supply of services, receipt of interest, rents, royalties or dividends, other than increases relating to contributions from equity participants. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover"]

In determining whether a person meets the threshold of being a small company, the value of the supply of a capital asset of the person is excluded from taxable supplies. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

In that same determination, the value of a supply made solely as a consequence of the person selling the whole or a part of its business or permanently ceasing to carry on business is also excluded. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- No statute named the Nigeria Small Business Tax Act 2025 is among the passages.
- The passages give different turnover limits for a small business and a small company, and do not say which applies to a particular taxpayer.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "gross turnover" (gazette pages A 504, A 505)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10) (gazette page A 277)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": A small business has gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less in the cited print and ₦50,000,000 or less in the Gombe print. (DR-267)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business": Total fixed assets must be less than ₦250,000,000 in the cited text and not more than ₦250,000,000 in the National Assembly text, so exactly ₦250,000,000 qualifies only under the National Assembly text. (DR-270)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-references: subsection (4), sections 105 and 107 (cited) against subsection (5), sections 100 and 102 (National Assembly). (DR-198)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10): Cross-reference: section 152 of the Nigeria Tax Act (cited) against section 151 (National Assembly text, the same section under its numbering, DR-000). (DR-199)

claims.text: A taxable person shall, for value added tax, with or without a notice, and whether or not an economic activity has taken place, submit a return to the Service in the prescribed form, on or before the 21st day of the following month.
Where the Service grants an extension of the period for filing returns under section 22, the extension does not imply an extension of time to pay the tax.
The returns shall contain the input tax paid, output tax collected and value added tax payable in respect of all taxable supplies in the preceding month.
For the purpose of attribution, any return under section 22 shall provide details of consumption of taxable supplies, irrespective of where the return is filed.
Where technology is deployed by the Service, a taxable person shall render returns in real time or at such other time as the Service may prescribe.
The filing rule in section 22(1) shall not apply to a small business.

Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Taxpayer Identification ("Tax ID") for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4]

A non-resident person that supplies taxable goods or services to any person in Nigeria, or derives income from Nigeria, shall register for tax purposes and obtain a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 6]

A non-resident person who derives only passive income from investment in Nigeria may not be required to register for tax, but shall provide relevant information as may be prescribed by the Service. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 6]

Every ministry, department or agency of the Federal or a State government, and every Local Government, shall register for tax and obtain a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 5]

"Registration" means the action or process of registering or of being registered for tax purposes in accordance with the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "registration"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether the asker is a taxable person, a non-resident person, or a government body, so whether the asker must register cannot be determined.
- The passages do not define "taxable person" in a way that shows whether a small business falls within it.

- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "registration" (gazette page A 331)

A taxable person who fails or refuses to file returns, or knowingly files incomplete or inaccurate returns, to the relevant tax authority in accordance with the Act is liable to an administrative penalty of ₦100,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

The same provision adds an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 101]

Where any tax is not paid within the period prescribed under the Act, and subject to section 67 of the Act, a sum equal to 10% of the amount of the tax payable is added to it, and interest also runs on the tax due from the date it becomes payable until it is paid. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

The 10% sum and the interest under that section are not deemed part of the tax paid for the purpose of claiming relief under the Act or any other tax law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 65]

- The passages do not say whether section 101 applies to a VAT return in particular, or what the filing deadline for a VAT return is.

The rule applies notwithstanding any provision of this Act or any other enactment.

cases.rendered:
Where, in any year of assessment, the effective tax rate of a company is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

This rule applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

"Effective tax rate" means the aggregate covered tax paid by a company for a year of assessment divided by the profits of the company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

"Profits" for this purpose means the net profits before tax as reported in the audited financial statement less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost for the year. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

The rule applies notwithstanding any provision of this Act or any other enactment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The top-up amount needs a calculation, which is not done here: the profits figure under the section's definition, the covered tax paid, and the gap to 15%.
- The question gives profits of a stated amount, but the section defines profits as net profits before tax in the audited financial statement less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. The depreciation and personnel cost figures are not given.
- Whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group is not shown. The passages do not say what makes a company a constituent entity or part of an MNE group, so the passages do not confirm that 'large multinational group' meets this test.
- The passages do not state the aggregate covered tax paid, which the effective tax rate definition uses.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The 15% minimum effective tax rate applies from an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 in the gazette and ₦50,000,000,000 in the National Assembly text. (DR-053)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The National Assembly text exempts approved free-zone enterprises (except for sales into the customs territory and MNE entities) and lets the Service set a higher turnover threshold by regulation; the gazette has neither and measures turnover in the relevant year of assessment rather than the financial year. (DR-054)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette numbers the subsections (1), (2) and (4), with no (3); the labels are kept as printed. The National Assembly text has (1) to (4). (DR-055)

There is no further tax charged on a dividend received by a non-resident from a Nigerian company, other than tax deducted at source under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 19]

Nothing in the Act gives the non-resident, or the Nigerian company paying the dividend, a right to repayment of tax paid under section 51 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 19]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether the Netherlands parent company counts as a non-resident under the Act.
- Section 51 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, which the passages refer to for the deduction at source, is not among the passages, so the rate and the way the deduction works are not stated.
- Any tax treaty effect on the deduction is not covered by the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 19 (gazette page A 408)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 7 (gazette page A 396)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 19: Cross-reference: section 51 (gazette) against section 50 (National Assembly) of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act. (DR-027)

cases.rationale: nta2025:s164: donations to religious, charitable and educational institutions in Nigeria are deductible (subsection (3)(c)), capped at 10% of profit before tax (subsection (5)), with evidence required (subsection (4)).
cases.question: Our company gave money to a church school's building fund. Can we deduct that donation, and is there a limit?

claims.text: For working out a company's profits or loss from any source chargeable to tax under Chapter Two, the amount of any donation made for that period by the company to any fund, body or institution in Nigeria to which section 164 applies is deducted, subject to that section.
Section 164 applies to donations made to religious, charitable, educational and scientific institutions, established in Nigeria.
A donation under section 164 may be deducted from the profits of that period even if the donation is of a revenue or capital nature.
A company making a deduction for a donation shall provide the requisite document evidencing the donation to the relevant tax authority.
The total deduction allowed to a company under section 164 for any year of assessment shall not exceed an amount equal to 10% of the company's profit before tax for that year.
For a donation other than in cash, the value for section 164 is the lower of the market value at the time of the donation or the consideration paid for the item when it was acquired.

gaps: The passages do not say whether a church school is a religious or educational institution established in Nigeria, or whether its building fund is a fund or body to which section 164 applies.
The passages do not say whether the donation was in cash.
Working out the 10% limit on the company's actual profit before tax is a calculation the passages do not do.

cases.rationale: ntaa2025:s72 subsections (2) to (4): banks and government bodies demand a certificate for the three years before the current year of assessment for the listed transactions.
cases.question: Why would my bank ask for a tax clearance certificate, and how many years must it cover?

claims.text: Any commercial bank with which a person has any dealing in respect of the transactions listed in subsection (4) shall demand from that person a tax clearance certificate of three years immediately preceding the current year of assessment.

The listed transactions are: application for certificate of occupancy, approval of building plans, application for award of contract by government or its agencies, application for firearms licence, application for import and export licence, and application for trade licence.

A tax clearance certificate shall disclose, in respect of the last three years of assessment, the total profits or chargeable income, the tax payable, the tax paid, and the tax outstanding or alternatively a statement that no tax is due.

Where the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that tax assessed has been fully paid or that no tax is due, it shall issue the certificate within two weeks of the person's demand or, if not, give reasons for the denial.

cases.rendered:
Every taxable person shall register with the relevant tax authority and obtain a Tax ID for the purpose of compliance with tax obligations. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 4]

A taxable person who fails or refuses to register for tax under section 4 is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦50,000 in the first month in which the failure occurs and ₦25,000 for each subsequent month in which the failure continues. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A relevant tax authority may, based on the information available to it, register and issue a Tax ID to a person who should apply for a Tax ID but failed to do so. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

The relevant tax authority shall promptly notify a person registered and issued with a Tax ID in this way of the registration and Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 7]

A Tax ID is to be a condition for entering into a contract with any federal or state ministry, department or agency and local government. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

A statutory body or company that awards a contract to an unregistered person is liable to pay an administrative penalty of ₦5,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 100]

A person engaged in banking, insurance, stock-broking or other financial services in Nigeria shall ensure that every taxable person provides a Tax ID. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 8]

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company, and for a small company the rate is 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company means a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Any company other than a small company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)

cases.question: We bought ₦9 million of office furniture. How much capital allowance can we claim each year?

claims.text: Capital expenditure on furniture and fittings, including those used in vessels, ships, aircraft, trains, plants and buildings, for the purposes of trade or business is qualifying furniture and fittings expenditure.
Furniture and Fittings Expenditure is in Class 2, which has a rate of 20%.

Where a person has incurred qualifying expenditure wholly and exclusively for the purposes of its trade or business, an allowance is made for each year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for that trade or business, at the rate in Table I.
The allowance is made for a year of assessment if, at the end of a basis period, the person owns the asset and used it for the purposes of its trade or business.
Where the basis period for a year of assessment is less than one year, the allowance for that year is granted proportionately.

An amount of 1% of qualifying capital expenditure is recorded in the capital allowance computation schedule for statistical purposes until the asset is disposed of. It is a notional amount and does not increase or reduce the capital allowance claimable.
Residue of qualifying expenditure is the total qualifying expenditure on the asset up to the date, less the total capital allowance made on that asset before that date.
An allowance is not made for a year unless it is claimed for that year, or the relevant tax authority is of the opinion that it would be just to the taxpayer and reasonable to do so.
Where an allowance is not claimed in the year of assessment in the basis period for which the asset was used for the trade or business, it is carried forward to a subsequent period.

The allowance is subtracted from the remainder of the assessable profits or income for the year. Where there is no remainder or an insufficient remainder, the deduction, or the part not yet made, is treated as a deduction for the next year and succeeding years until fully utilised.

Where an owner partly uses an asset for a trade or business, the allowance is apportioned to the trade or business as may be reasonable. The relevant tax authority makes adjustments it deems fit if it considers the basis of apportionment not just and reasonable.

gaps: The rupee amount of the yearly allowance needs a calculation applying the rate to the cost, which is not done here.
The passages do not say that the office furniture in the question is furniture and fittings expenditure for the purposes of trade or business.
The passages do not say whether the asset is in use at the end of the basis period, or whether it is used wholly for the business.

Where the Service grants an extension of time to file returns, this does not extend the time to pay the tax.

cases.rendered:
A taxable person must, not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, remit to the Service the excess where output VAT exceeds input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess as a credit against subsequent months. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

VAT paid by a taxable person to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152]

VAT collected by a taxable person on making taxable supplies is called output VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154]

A taxable person must submit a VAT return to the Service in the prescribed form on or before the 21st day of the following month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The return must show the input tax paid, output tax collected and VAT payable on all taxable supplies in the preceding month. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

The requirement to submit a monthly VAT return does not apply to a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Where the Service grants an extension of time to file returns, this does not extend the time to pay the tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 22(1) to (10)]

Input tax may be deducted only to the extent it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies. Where input tax relates to both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to taxable supplies may be deducted. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

- The amount payable needs a subtraction of input VAT from output VAT, which is not done here.

Where any payment is made to a person, the person making the payment shall, at the date when payment is made or otherwise settled, deduct the tax at the rate prescribed in regulations relating to deduction of tax at source. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 51(1) to (7)]

Rent means payments of any kind, received or receivable, paid or payable, for the use of, or the right to use property or equipment of any kind, and includes remuneration for the use, letting, hire or use in any other form of movable or immovable property. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "rent"]

Regulations relating to deduction of tax at source apply for the purpose of giving effect to section 51. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 51(8) to (9)]

cases.rendered:
Notes
- State and local government taxes and levies are outside the corpus this tool covers (v1). Answers come only from the provisions that are in the corpus.

The Nigeria Revenue Service (the Service) has exclusive responsibility to administer taxes on companies. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1)]

The Service's exclusive responsibility to administer taxes as contained in the Act includes value added tax and exemptions from value added tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1)]

The Service also has power to administer income tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1)]

A company must file its self-assessment return with the Service, whether or not it is liable to pay tax. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 11(1) to (2)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say whether a state revenue office has any role in collecting a company's income tax.
- The passages do not say how a company's income tax payment should be made or to whom payment is made.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1) (gazette pages A 265, A 266)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 11(1) to (2) (gazette page A 269)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 3(1): In the cited text the Service has exclusive responsibility for the surcharge on fossil fuels; the National Assembly text omits it, and adds taxation of income from petroleum and value added tax to the taxes the Service has power to administer. (DR-179)

cases.rendered:
Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

A business providing professional services is not classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

The additional tax rule on companies with an effective tax rate below 15% applies to a constituent entity of an MNE group, and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the furniture company's turnover and fixed assets are as stated is a fact about the company, and the passages do not confirm it.
- The passages do not say whether selling furniture counts as providing professional services.
- The passages do not say whether the company is a constituent entity of an MNE group.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. National Assembly: covered taxes (companies income tax, petroleum profit tax, hydrocarbon tax, development levy, priority sector tax credit) as a percentage of net income, which excludes franked investment income and unrealised gains or losses. (DR-051)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The gazette applies the 15% minimum to every constituent entity of an MNE group; the National Assembly text only where the group's turnover is at least 750 million (printed with a pound sign) or its equivalent. (DR-052)

claims.text: An advance ruling may be issued to give clarity, consistency and certainty on how any tax law is interpreted and applied, as long as the ruling does not amend or replace the law.
The relevant tax authority may issue an advance ruling on application by a taxable person within 21 days of receiving the application, or give reasons in writing for being unable to issue the ruling.
An application must be made in the prescribed form and manner by a person who is a party to any tax related issue or transaction, or by two or more such parties.
The definition of advance ruling includes a written opinion or decision given to a taxpayer by the relevant tax authority on a transaction or proposed transaction, to give direction or clarification.

A company means a company as defined under the Companies and Allied Matters Act and a corporate body that may be formed under any other written law, and includes any association, whether incorporated in or outside Nigeria.

An application must contain the taxpayer's name, Tax ID, postal address, email address and telephone number, a complete description of the issue or transaction including any financial implications, and a complete description of its impact on the tax liability of the taxpayer or any connected person.

An application must also contain details of any ongoing audit, previous correspondence and decisions of the tax authority on the issue, the statutory provisions or legal basis relied on, the reasons the ruling should be granted, and a written statement on whether the matter is before any tribunal or court of competent jurisdiction.
The tax authority may request additional information from an applicant, and where necessary shall give the applicant a reasonable opportunity to make representations or provide clarifications.
An applicant may withdraw an application at any time before a ruling is issued.

The tax authority may reject an application where it requires an opinion, conclusion or determination on the laws of a foreign country, an issue already before a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, the interpretation of the Constitution, an issue that is academic, hypothetical, frivolous or vexatious, or a ruling that will interfere substantially with an ongoing audit, investigation or other proceeding involving the applicant or connected persons.
A ruling is limited in effect to the applicant and the transaction for which it is given, and it is rendered on a set of facts before the tax authority and cannot be of general application.

A ruling is void where the transaction actually carried out is materially different from the one described, where there is fraud, misrepresentation or non-disclosure of a material fact, or where an assumption made or condition imposed by the tax authority is not satisfied or carried out by the taxpayer.

A ruling ceases to be effective where the tax law provision it concerned is repealed or amended in a way that materially affects it, or where a court overturns or modifies the interpretation of the tax law on which it is based.

A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company"]

Under the rates of tax for companies, a small company is taxed at 0% on its total profits, and any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

The Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 separately defines a small business as one that earns gross turnover of ₦100,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets less than ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small business. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business"]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The comparison of the company's turnover figure with the small company turnover limit is left to the reader, as the passages do not apply it.
- The passages do not say whether a catering company counts as a business providing professional services.
- The passages do not say whether the small business definition in the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 applies to income tax rates for companies; the rate section refers only to a small company.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company" (gazette page A 510)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 147, definition of "small business" (gazette page A 331)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)

cases.question: A firm in Ghana does our bookkeeping remotely. Do we have to deal with VAT on its fees?

claims.text: A taxable person must pay VAT to a supplier on the taxable supply made to that person, and the VAT paid is known as input VAT.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom a taxable supply is made in Nigeria, and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.
Self-accounted VAT is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service.

The remission of self-accounted VAT is to be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates.

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six must keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person.

The Federal, State and Local Governments and their Ministries, Departments or Agencies, and any other person appointed by the Service, must collect or withhold VAT on taxable supplies made to them and remit it to the Service.

gaps: The passages do not say whether bookkeeping services supplied remotely by a firm outside Nigeria are a taxable supply made in Nigeria.
The passages do not say whether the business is a taxable person or has been appointed by the Service to collect or withhold VAT.
The passages do not say whether the Service has directed the business to self-account, or whether the Ghanaian firm's invoice includes VAT.
The passages contain no rule on the place of supply or on VAT for non-resident suppliers, and no rate of VAT.

cases.rendered:

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom a taxable supply is made in Nigeria, and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

Self-accounted VAT is to be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction, or as may be prescribed by the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

The remission of self-accounted VAT is to be accompanied by a schedule showing the name, Tax ID and address of the contractor or supplier, invoice number, gross amount of invoice, amount of the VAT and the month to which the return relates. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

A person with an obligation to collect VAT under Chapter Six must keep proper records and make appropriate returns and remittances, and the compliance provisions apply to that person as though it is the taxable person. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

The Federal, State and Local Governments and their Ministries, Departments or Agencies, and any other person appointed by the Service, must collect or withhold VAT on taxable supplies made to them and remit it to the Service. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 155]

cases.rendered:
VAT that a taxable person pays to a supplier on taxable supplies made to the person is called input VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152]

VAT that a taxable person collects on making taxable supplies is called output VAT. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154]

Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person is entitled to use the excess tax as a credit against subsequent months. This is to be done not later than the due date for rendering the relevant tax return prescribed by the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

A taxable person is entitled to a refund of excess VAT not used as a credit, upon request to the Service and provision of such information or documents as the Service may require. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Input tax on a taxable supply, including services and fixed assets, may be deducted from the tax payable on taxable supplies at the end of the tax period in which the supply occurred, but only to the extent that it was incurred for consumption, use or supply in the course of making taxable supplies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Where input tax is incurred in making both taxable and non-taxable supplies, only the proportion relating to making taxable supplies may be deducted. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Input tax is allowable for deduction within five years after the end of the tax period in which it was incurred. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

The input tax that may be deducted is limited to taxable supplies made as from the commencement of this Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the question's purchases and sales are taxable supplies, and how much of the input VAT relates to taxable supplies, is not stated in the passages.
- The amount of any credit or refund would need a calculation, which is not done here.
- The due date for the return under the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 is not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 152 (gazette page A 473)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154 (gazette page A 474)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156 (gazette pages A 474, A 475)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 154: Cross-reference: the rate is in section 148 (gazette); the National Assembly text cites section 146, which is not its rate section (147). (DR-061)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156: The gazette lets a person whose supplies are zero-rated pay VAT on its inputs and then claim a refund; the National Assembly text has no such subsection. (DR-067)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 156: Because of the gazette's extra subsection (4), gazette (5) and (6) are National Assembly (4) and (5). (DR-068)

claims.text: A non-resident person who makes taxable supplies to Nigeria shall register for tax and include VAT on its invoice for all taxable supplies.

Where a non-resident person makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the taxable person to whom the supply is made in Nigeria shall withhold the VAT due on the supply and remit it to the Service.
The Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier of taxable supplies, to collect the VAT and remit it to the Service.

Where a person appointed by the Service has made a taxable supply to a taxable person in Nigeria, the taxable person shall not have the obligation to withhold the VAT, except where the appointed person has failed to collect the VAT.
A non-resident person that makes a taxable supply to a person in Nigeria may appoint a representative for the purpose of compliance with its VAT obligations.

The Service may direct a taxable person to whom taxable supplies are made in Nigeria and who was issued an invoice on which VAT is not included, to self-account for the VAT payable and remit it to the Service.

VAT collected, withheld or self-accounted under section 155 shall be remitted to the Service on or before the 14th day of the month immediately following the month of the transaction or as may be prescribed by the Service.
Government bodies and any other person appointed by the Service to collect or withhold VAT shall collect or withhold VAT on taxable supplies made to them and remit it to the Service.

VAT is generally charged on the value of all taxable supplies at the rate of 7.5%, subject to the provisions of Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 148]

VAT shall be paid on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 145]

"Basic food items" means an agriculture-based or aquatic-based staple food including cereals such as maize, rice, wheat, millet, barley, sorghum, oats, fonio and finer millet, in the form of grain, flour, crop, whether raw or semi-processed, whether in bulk or retail. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 189, definition of "basic food items", paragraphs (a) to (k)]

"Basic food items" also includes flour and starch, including cassava flakes (garri), whether bleached or unbleached, refined or unrefined, provided that it is suitable for culinary purposes. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 189, definition of "basic food items", paragraphs (a) to (k)]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- Whether the rice and garri sold in the shop are a taxable supply, and whether they fit the printed forms and conditions of the definition, is not stated in the passages.
- Paragraph 2 of the Thirtenth Schedule, to which the 0% rate is subject, is not among the passages.
- Whether the shop's sales fall under any other provision of the Act is not stated in the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 187 (gazette pages A 490, A 491)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 148 (gazette page A 472)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 145 (gazette page A 470)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 187: Cross-reference: the gazette refers to paragraph 2 of the 'Thirtenth' Schedule, which has no paragraph 2; the National Assembly text refers to the Tenth Schedule. (DR-081)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 187: The gazette zero-rates electric vehicles and parts and semi-knock-down units for assembling them; the National Assembly text does not list them. (DR-082)

VAT is payable on all taxable supplies in Nigeria, subject to the exemptions in Part IV of Chapter Eight of the Act.

VAT is not to be collected on the items specified in paragraph 1 of the Eleventh Schedule, except where the Minister by an order published in the Official Gazette specifies the date of collection of VAT on the items listed in the order.

claims.text: A small company is a company that earns gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less per annum with total fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, provided that any business providing professional services shall not be classified as a small company.

Professional services are services provided by an individual or a firm having specialised knowledge, skills, and qualifications in specific fields, including consulting, planning, or support services, excluding artisans or vocational services.

Low turnover alone does not settle the matter, because the definition of small company excludes any business providing professional services, and the definition of professional services lists consulting.
A small company is taxed at 0% on its total profits for a year of assessment, while any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of the Act.

gaps: Whether the firm's own services count as professional services depends on facts about the firm that the passages do not contain.

Low turnover alone does not settle the matter, because the definition of small company excludes any business providing professional services, and the definition of professional services lists consulting. Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": A small company has gross turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less in the gazette and ₦100,000,000 or less in the National Assembly text, which also says 'business' instead of 'company'. (DR-150)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "small company": The gazette excludes any business providing professional services from being a small company; the National Assembly text has no such exclusion. (DR-151)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "professional services": Only the gazette defines 'professional services', the term that excludes a business from being a small company. (DR-138)

claims.text: For companies, the definition of "connected persons" says a company is connected to another company where the same person has control over both companies, or connected persons acting separately have control over the companies.
Two companies are connected where one company participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other company.
Two companies are also connected where the same persons participate directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of a company and another company.

In other cases, two persons are connected where one may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions, or wishes of the other, or both may reasonably be expected to act that way for a third person, or one has the practical ability to control the business decisions of the other.
Two persons are not connected solely because one is the employee or client of the other, or both are employees or clients of a third person.
"Related parties" has the same meaning as connected persons.

gaps: The passages do not define "control", so when a person has control over a company is not stated.
Whether the facts of the owner's companies meet any of these tests cannot be decided from the passages.

For companies, the definition of "connected persons" says a company is connected to another company where the same person has control over both companies, or connected persons acting separately have control over the companies. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

Two companies are connected where one company participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

Two companies are also connected where the same persons participate directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of a company and another company. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

In other cases, two persons are connected where one may reasonably be expected to act in accordance with the directions, requests, suggestions, or wishes of the other, or both may reasonably be expected to act that way for a third person, or one has the practical ability to control the business decisions of the other. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

Two persons are not connected solely because one is the employee or client of the other, or both are employees or clients of a third person. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "connected persons"]

"Related parties" has the same meaning as connected persons. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 202, definition of "related parties"]

claims.text: Where the relevant tax authority discovers or is of the opinion, at any time, that a taxable person liable to tax has not been assessed or has been assessed at an amount less than ought to have been charged, it may, within six years of the assessment, assess the taxable person at the amount or additional amount that ought to have been charged.

Despite the time limit in subsection (1), where there is a deliberate misstatement by a taxable person in connection with any tax imposed under the Nigeria Tax Act, 2025 or any other tax law, the relevant tax authority may at any time, and as often as may be necessary, assess the taxable person for the amount needed to make good any loss of tax attributable to the deliberate misstatement.

All relevant facts are to be considered in computing the additional amount of tax, even where those facts were not known when a prior assessment or additional assessment was made for the taxable person in the same year.
The provisions of the Act on notice of assessment, appeal and other proceedings apply to an additional assessment and to the tax charged.

Section 41 does not prevent the tax authority from making an assessment or additional assessment for any year that does not involve re-opening any issue on the same facts which has been determined for that year of assessment under section 41(5) by agreement or on appeal.

cases.rendered:
Where the taxable person has given notice of an objection or appeal, collection of tax remains in abeyance until the objection or appeal is determined. This is subject to section 11 of the Act. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

The taxable person shall pay the tax that is not the subject of an objection or appeal. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Tax charged by an assessment that is not or has not been the subject of an objection or appeal is payable within 30 days of service of the notice of assessment, after deduction of any amount to be set off for collection purposes or any amount deposited against the tax. The relevant tax authority may, in its discretion, extend the time for payment. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

After an objection or appeal is determined, the relevant tax authority shall serve a notice of the tax payable as determined. That tax is payable within 30 days of the date of service of the notice. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

Any balance of tax unpaid as at the due date attracts interest and penalties as provided in the Act or any other relevant law. [Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025, section 49(1) to (6)]

cases.question: My company made ₦120 million profit this year. How much company income tax will it pay?

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of this Act.

Where the effective tax rate of a company in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment.

Tax is levied for each year of assessment on the total profits of every company. A small company is taxed at 0%. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

Any other company is taxed at the rate of 30 per cent from the commencement of this Act. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56]

The total profits of a company are its total assessable profits from all sources, including chargeable gains, less any loss ascertained in accordance with subsection (6) and capital allowance in accordance with Part I of the First Schedule. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4)]

Where the effective tax rate of a company in a year of assessment is less than 15%, the company shall recompute and pay an additional tax that makes its effective tax rate equal to 15%. This applies to a company that is a constituent entity of an MNE group and to any other company with an aggregate turnover of ₦20,000,000,000 and above in the relevant year of assessment. [Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57]

Not covered by the retrieved provisions:
- The passages do not say what makes a company a small company, so it is not known whether the company is taxed at 0% or at 30 per cent.
- The passages do not say whether the ₦120 million is the company's total profits after losses and capital allowance, so the taxable amount is not known.
- The tax calculation itself is not done here.
- Whether the company's turnover or MNE group status brings it within the effective tax rate rule is not known.
- Section 27(6), which section 27(1) refers to for losses, and Part I of the First Schedule are not among the passages.

Sources
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56 (gazette page A 426)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4) (gazette pages A 412, A 413)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57 (gazette page A 426)

Differences between official texts
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 56: The National Assembly text lets the President, on the advice of the National Economic Council, reduce the 30% rate to 25% by order; the gazette has no such provision. (DR-050)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 27(1) to (4): The National Assembly text requires companies in the priority sector to obtain a certificate of acceptance from the Industrial Inspectorate Department for qualifying capital expenditure; the gazette has no such condition. (DR-039)
- Nigeria Tax Act 2025, section 57: The minimum tax is measured differently. Gazette: covered tax paid divided by profits, where profits are net profit before tax less 5% of depreciation and personnel cost. cases.question: Under section 191 of the Nigeria Tax Act, where do objections and appeals go?

claims.text: Section 191 says the provisions on objections and appeals under Chapter Four of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025 apply to a direction made under that section.

A direction under section 191 is one the relevant tax authority may make where it is of the opinion that a transaction which reduces or may reduce tax payable is artificial or fictitious, or that a disposition is not given effect to.

gaps: Chapter Four of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act, 2025, which section 191 refers to, is not among the passages, so where objections and appeals under it go is not shown.
The passages on objections and appeals in section 41 of the Nigeria Tax Administration Act are in Chapter Two, and the passages do not say that they apply to section 191 directions.
